decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is only now reaching release in Q1/2019, so its results cannot yet be judged against aspirations, and the firm's slack in its established dosimetry business allows it to carry this strategic platform product.
Small volume chambers are core consumables in the firm's dosimetry line with low carrying costs, and there is no reported shortfall that would trigger problemistic search.
A second small volume chamber adds some overlap risk, but one year is too early for evidence of underperformance, and the portfolio breadth fits customer needs for detector variety.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple for reference dosimetry and accredited calibration workflows, so it likely meets aspiration levels.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the water phantom and scanning systems, supporting the integrated QA platform, and shows no sign of failure.
Thimble chambers are established, low-risk products with steady clinical demand, so dropping one would release few resources.
